sources.entry: File Architect - Create file and folder structures from plain text descriptions.

summary.one_liner: File Architect is a desktop app (built with Tauri, React and Vite) that creates file and folder structures from plain text descriptions.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes File Architect as a desktop application that creates file and folder structures from plain text. The repository holds the core app code, built with Tauri (Rust and TypeScript), React, Vite and shadcn/ui components. It includes pnpm-based dev and build commands, a Windows ARM64 development setup, and a cross-compile script for producing a Windows x64 executable from macOS. Licensing checks send a machine ID to filearchitect.com, and a development-only override lets testers simulate trial, lifetime and yearly licenses. The README does not describe the text syntax used to define structures.
use_cases: create many files and folders quickly
build file trees from a plain text outline
notable: Creates file and folder trees from plain text input
Tauri desktop app with a React and Vite front end
Cross-compiles a Windows x64 exe from macOS using xwin and LLVM
Development-only license override for trial, lifetime and yearly modes
Includes an in-app updater path using minisign signatures
caveats: Trial use is limited to a set number of lines, and licensing requires contacting filearchitect.com
Windows ARM64 and cross-compile builds need extra toolchain setup (MSVC, LLVM, xwin, b2 CLI)
Cross-compiling from macOS produces only the .exe, with no installer
